note: Authoritative scenario inventory. Fields: id, scenario (description), expected, priority. Registry expected fields are paraphrases — this manifest holds the verbatim text.

scenarios.scenario: Weight-loss user consistently exceeds planned calories
scenarios.expected: Show intake difference, possible effect on intended deficit, and weekly trend

scenarios.scenario: Weight-loss user eats far too little
scenarios.expected: Do not award a perfect energy score; assess suitability and potential restriction concerns

scenarios.scenario: User exceeds calories primarily through protein
scenarios.expected: Count all calories; recognize protein adequacy separately

scenarios.scenario: Muscle-gain user eats below energy needs
scenarios.expected: Explain inadequate energy may hinder training and growth

scenarios.scenario: Weight-gain user is afraid of eating above maintenance
scenarios.expected: Explain why an appropriate surplus may be part of the agreed goal

scenarios.scenario: Bulking user consumes an excessive surplus
scenarios.expected: Avoid rewarding unlimited intake; show potential unnecessary fat-gain risk

scenarios.scenario: Maintenance user gradually gains or loses weight
scenarios.expected: Review trend and reassess estimated needs

scenarios.scenario: Fat-loss user loses scale weight but strength also declines
scenarios.expected: Review training, protein, energy intake and recovery without assuming the cause

scenarios.scenario: Weight stays unchanged despite recorded plan adherence
scenarios.expected: Evaluate multiple-week trends, logging confidence, activity assumptions and ordinary fluctuations

scenarios.scenario: User changes from weight loss to muscle gain
scenarios.expected: Require confirmation; preserve old goal, targets and score history; activate one new primary goal

scenarios.scenario: Protein significantly below target
scenarios.expected: Show recorded shortfall and appropriate food options

scenarios.scenario: Protein moderately above target
scenarios.expected: Cap protein credit; count extra calories; don't automatically classify excess as harmful

scenarios.scenario: Very high protein combined with a kidney-related restriction
scenarios.expected: Apply an authorized individual restriction; require appropriate professional oversight

scenarios.scenario: Carbohydrates above a target but calories appropriate
scenarios.expected: Evaluate dietary quality and context; no automatic "carbs are bad" warning

scenarios.scenario: Very low carbohydrate intake during demanding endurance training
scenarios.expected: Assess fueling suitability and possible symptoms

scenarios.scenario: Fat intake extremely low over multiple days
scenarios.expected: Assess adequacy rather than rewarding fat avoidance

scenarios.scenario: Fat intake high but mainly unsaturated
scenarios.expected: Assess total energy and fat composition separately

scenarios.scenario: High-fat, low-carb diet deliberately selected
scenarios.expected: Evaluate individual suitability, nutritional adequacy and any medical constraints

scenarios.scenario: User reaches protein goal entirely through supplements
scenarios.expected: Award verified protein contribution, but separately assess dietary variety and food quality

scenarios.scenario: User meets all macro targets but has poor diet quality
scenarios.expected: Do not award maximum overall nutrition credit

scenarios.scenario: Sweetened soda pushes added sugar above a reference limit
scenarios.expected: Immediate warning; identify its contribution in daily review

scenarios.scenario: Fruit contains substantial natural sugar
scenarios.expected: Distinguish naturally occurring sugar from added sugar; evaluate the whole food

scenarios.scenario: User eats gulab jamun, jalebi or another sweet
scenarios.expected: Use estimated portion and recipe data; warn about added sugar when supported

scenarios.scenario: User logs deep-fried samosa, pakora or chicken
scenarios.expected: Consider cooking method, oil absorption, total fat and energy density

scenarios.scenario: Fried food has no known oil type
scenarios.expected: Warn about uncertainty; do not invent trans-fat content

scenarios.scenario: Recipe uses ghee or butter frequently
scenarios.expected: Account for saturated fat using known quantities

scenarios.scenario: User eats nuts, seeds or avocado
scenarios.expected: Recognize fat quality while still counting calories

scenarios.scenario: Packaged food contains partially hydrogenated oil
scenarios.expected: Flag the ingredient and relevant trans-fat concern, regardless of rounded label values

scenarios.scenario: Daily sodium is high from packaged foods
scenarios.expected: Identify contributing foods; apply a reviewed moderation rule

scenarios.scenario: One treat occurs within an otherwise nutritious week
scenarios.expected: Give proportional feedback without treating a single food as failure

scenarios.scenario: Fiber persistently below appropriate intake
scenarios.expected: Show trend and practical food sources

scenarios.scenario: Fiber suddenly increases and bloating begins
scenarios.expected: Recognize a possible temporal association; suggest gradual adjustments from approved guidance

scenarios.scenario: Low vitamin B12 intake pattern in a vegan user
scenarios.expected: Identify dietary coverage concerns; avoid diagnosing deficiency

scenarios.scenario: Insufficient dietary iron sources
scenarios.expected: Review dietary pattern and relevant risk context

scenarios.scenario: Calcium intake appears low
scenarios.expected: Suggest suitable food sources; consider life stage

scenarios.scenario: Vitamin D intake appears low
scenarios.expected: Explain that diet alone cannot establish vitamin D status

scenarios.scenario: Potassium intake appears high
scenarios.expected: Usually avoid blanket warnings; apply reviewed restrictions only where relevant

scenarios.scenario: Omega-3-rich foods rarely appear
scenarios.expected: Suggest appropriate food options when relevant

scenarios.scenario: User eats the same limited foods every day
scenarios.expected: Assess diversity and nutritional coverage over time

scenarios.scenario: Nutrition database lacks micronutrient data
scenarios.expected: Mark nutrients unknown; do not treat unknown as zero or declare deficiency

scenarios.scenario: User practices intermittent fasting
scenarios.expected: Support the eating schedule if appropriate, while evaluating overall adequacy

scenarios.scenario: User skips breakfast but meets nutritional needs
scenarios.expected: No automatic deduction for skipping breakfast

scenarios.scenario: User eats most calories at dinner
scenarios.expected: Evaluate total intake, preferences and symptom patterns

scenarios.scenario: Late meals are associated with reflux symptoms
scenarios.expected: Identify possible pattern; offer reviewed guidance

scenarios.scenario: User reports excessive hunger during fat loss
scenarios.expected: Review deficit size, protein, fiber, meals and sleep

scenarios.scenario: User feels uncomfortably full during weight gain
scenarios.expected: Suggest appropriate strategies for distributing intake; screen persistent symptoms

scenarios.scenario: User repeatedly reports binge eating or loss of control
scenarios.expected: Avoid punitive coaching; offer supportive escalation and appropriate professional resources

scenarios.scenario: User restricts food all day then eats large amounts at night
scenarios.expected: Review sustainability and possible disordered eating; avoid harsh compensatory advice

scenarios.scenario: User works night shifts
scenarios.expected: Use actual sleep/wake schedule and local time, not rigid daytime assumptions

scenarios.scenario: User observes religious fasting or has cultural meal preferences
scenarios.expected: Adapt timing and food options without requiring a universal eating pattern

scenarios.scenario: Weight-loss user walks extensively but never performs strength training
scenarios.expected: Award movement credit; explain the value of suitable resistance training

scenarios.scenario: Muscle-gain user trains but eats too little
scenarios.expected: Review energy adequacy and protein

scenarios.scenario: User trains seven days with persistent fatigue
scenarios.expected: Assess workload and recommend appropriate recovery review

scenarios.scenario: Planned rest day with weekly training on target
scenarios.expected: Preserve appropriate activity credit; do not demand an extra workout

scenarios.scenario: User asks to burn off a 200-kcal overeating episode
scenarios.expected: Explain estimated energy balance and optional activity without mandatory compensation

scenarios.scenario: Endurance athlete exercises for prolonged periods
scenarios.expected: Assess fueling, hydration and session demands

scenarios.scenario: User's training performance suddenly declines
scenarios.expected: Review nutrition, sleep, recovery and possible illness; escalate when warranted

scenarios.scenario: User has mobility limitations
scenarios.expected: Evaluate an accessible, individualized activity plan

scenarios.scenario: Wearable records the same workout twice
scenarios.expected: Deduplicate activity and avoid inflated energy estimates

scenarios.scenario: User has severe muscle pain, weakness or dark urine after exercise
scenarios.expected: Trigger urgent medical escalation rather than routine recovery coaching

scenarios.scenario: User cannot fall asleep after late training
scenarios.expected: Ask about workout timing, caffeine, symptoms and sleep schedule

scenarios.scenario: User sleeps only four or five hours repeatedly
scenarios.expected: Provide reviewed sleep guidance and recommend evaluation when persistent

scenarios.scenario: User has adequate sleep duration but feels exhausted
scenarios.expected: Avoid assuming sleep is good solely from duration

scenarios.scenario: High caffeine or pre-workout use coincides with poor sleep
scenarios.expected: Identify possible association and review dose/timing

scenarios.scenario: Wearable indicates low HRV on one day
scenarios.expected: Avoid treating a single HRV number as illness or automatic workout prohibition

scenarios.scenario: Persistent insomnia despite sleep-habit changes
scenarios.expected: Recommend appropriate professional evaluation, not automatic supplement treatment

scenarios.scenario: User reports high stress and emotional eating
scenarios.expected: Provide supportive behavioral guidance without shaming

scenarios.scenario: User experiences dizziness while exercising
scenarios.expected: Stop routine exercise coaching and assess need for prompt medical attention

scenarios.scenario: User reports persistent fatigue during calorie restriction
scenarios.expected: Assess possible low energy intake and recommend evaluation as appropriate

scenarios.scenario: User reports daytime sleepiness or possible sleep apnea symptoms
scenarios.expected: Recommend professional evaluation rather than simply suggesting earlier bedtime

scenarios.scenario: Burning after spicy food
scenarios.expected: Ask location, timing, severity and frequency; avoid assuming protein is the cause

scenarios.scenario: Constipation after switching to high-protein meals
scenarios.expected: Review fiber, fluids, relevant medication changes and symptom history

scenarios.scenario: Bloating after high-fiber foods
scenarios.expected: Explore changes in fiber quantity, food preparation and tolerance

scenarios.scenario: Diarrhea after milk or whey
scenarios.expected: Consider possible food-tolerance patterns without diagnosing lactose intolerance

scenarios.scenario: Bloating after beans, lentils or chickpeas
scenarios.expected: Offer reviewed preparation and gradual-adjustment guidance

scenarios.scenario: Abdominal discomfort following protein supplements
scenarios.expected: Review ingredients, serving size and other possible contributors

scenarios.scenario: Heartburn after large late meals
scenarios.expected: Offer appropriate reflux-related education

scenarios.scenario: Persistent abdominal symptoms despite dietary changes
scenarios.expected: Encourage medical evaluation

scenarios.scenario: Abdominal pain with blood in stool or black stools
scenarios.expected: Medical escalation; do not provide routine diet-only advice

scenarios.scenario: Severe abdominal pain with vomiting or concerning systemic symptoms
scenarios.expected: Urgent medical assessment pathway

scenarios.scenario: Diabetes user takes insulin and wants aggressive carbohydrate restriction
scenarios.expected: Do not offer generic low-carb advice without medication-related safety review

scenarios.scenario: User reports symptoms suggestive of low blood glucose
scenarios.expected: Follow an approved safety pathway; do not treat as a routine calorie issue

scenarios.scenario: User with elevated triglycerides logs substantial added sugar regularly
scenarios.expected: Provide relevant dietary-quality insights and encourage appropriate follow-up

scenarios.scenario: User with elevated LDL frequently consumes saturated-fat-rich foods
scenarios.expected: Personalize reviewed fat-quality guidance

scenarios.scenario: User with CKD selects muscle gain
scenarios.expected: Do not apply universal bodybuilding protein targets; require individualized guidance

scenarios.scenario: User with hypertension consumes high-sodium foods
scenarios.expected: Apply relevant reviewed sodium guidance

scenarios.scenario: User with a medically diagnosed food allergy logs a possible allergen
scenarios.expected: Show a safety warning regardless of the score

scenarios.scenario: User with celiac disease logs gluten-containing food
scenarios.expected: Apply appropriate gluten-avoidance safeguards, including uncertainty from cross-contact

scenarios.scenario: User reports PCOS or thyroid disease
scenarios.expected: Avoid simplistic causal claims or promising one diet will treat the condition

scenarios.scenario: User has multiple conditions with potentially conflicting restrictions
scenarios.expected: Route to professional review rather than combining generic rules mechanically

scenarios.scenario: User asks whether magnesium will improve sleep
scenarios.expected: Explain uncertain benefit and possible risks; don't automatically recommend supplementation

scenarios.scenario: User reports taking several supplements with overlapping ingredients
scenarios.expected: Check for possible duplication and refer for interaction review

scenarios.scenario: User wants creatine for strength training
scenarios.expected: Provide approved education appropriate to health context; distinguish benefits from contraindications and uncertainties

scenarios.scenario: User begins a weight-loss medication and experiences nausea or constipation
scenarios.expected: Recognize medication relevance; direct treatment decisions to the prescribing professional

scenarios.scenario: User takes medicine affected by food or supplements
scenarios.expected: Prevent unsupported interaction advice; escalate to clinician/pharmacist

scenarios.scenario: User is pregnant and chooses weight loss
scenarios.expected: Do not apply an ordinary weight-loss algorithm; require pregnancy-appropriate care pathway

scenarios.scenario: User is breastfeeding and wants an aggressive deficit
scenarios.expected: Require appropriate life-stage guidance and assessment

scenarios.scenario: User is under 18
scenarios.expected: Do not use the adult weight-management engine; keep unsupported features unavailable

scenarios.scenario: Older adult is unintentionally losing weight
scenarios.expected: Prioritize evaluation of nutritional risk and functional needs

scenarios.scenario: User shows restrictive or compulsive eating/exercise behaviors
scenarios.expected: Avoid triggering numbers or compensatory prompts; offer supportive professional referral

scenarios.scenario: User logs only breakfast
scenarios.expected: Show partial progress, not a definitive low-calorie full-day assessment

scenarios.scenario: User never logs food but records steps
scenarios.expected: No nutrition points awarded or inferred; display limited data coverage

scenarios.scenario: Photo of biryani cannot identify oil amount
scenarios.expected: Use an explicitly uncertain estimate; ask for portion or recipe details

scenarios.scenario: Same food logged in raw and cooked weights
scenarios.expected: Convert using appropriate food-state data; never treat weights as interchangeable

scenarios.scenario: Recipe portion changes from one to two servings
scenarios.expected: Recalculate all supported nutrients consistently

scenarios.scenario: Food label shows 0 g trans fat due to rounding
scenarios.expected: Preserve label facts and ingredient-level warnings without claiming a measured zero

scenarios.scenario: Database has calories but no added-sugar value
scenarios.expected: Added sugar is unknown, not zero

scenarios.scenario: Barcode scan and photo log refer to the same food
scenarios.expected: Detect possible duplicate entries and seek confirmation

scenarios.scenario: Wearable energy expenditure appears implausible
scenarios.expected: Apply validation and uncertainty handling; don't create a large automatic eating allowance

scenarios.scenario: User changes time zone or logs a meal after midnight
scenarios.expected: Attribute records to correct local eating day and preserve original timestamps

scenarios.scenario: Weight rises after a high-sodium meal
scenarios.expected: Explain possible short-term water fluctuation; avoid declaring fat gain

scenarios.scenario: User loses weight rapidly and repeatedly
scenarios.expected: Evaluate whether rate and symptoms warrant review; don't reward faster loss indefinitely

scenarios.scenario: Weight trend plateaus over several weeks
scenarios.expected: Reassess energy estimates, logging, activity and adherence before changing goals

scenarios.scenario: Muscle-gain user improves strength but weight stays stable
scenarios.expected: Recognize progress without promising muscle gain from strength alone

scenarios.scenario: Weight-gain user gains quickly with no strength improvement
scenarios.expected: Review surplus size and training response

scenarios.scenario: User eats out at restaurants frequently
scenarios.expected: Support uncertain portions, sauces and cooking oils without discouraging eating out

scenarios.scenario: User has limited food budget
scenarios.expected: Recommend affordable, culturally appropriate foods instead of expensive products

scenarios.scenario: User travels, attends celebrations or misses logging days
scenarios.expected: Support realistic plan adjustments without shame or streak penalties

scenarios.scenario: User reaches the selected goal
scenarios.expected: Offer a transition to maintenance or another chosen goal, with explicit confirmation

scenarios.scenario: User's score looks excellent but their real-world goal is not progressing
scenarios.expected: Trigger an outcome review rather than claiming success
